blocks.text: The module documentation identifies state.db as the local source of truth and explains directory, file, sidecar, SQLite durability, timestamp, transaction, and logging rules.
blocks.title: Local database contract

blocks.text: StoreError is the fixed local-store failure type. utc_now_iso creates UTC text and normalize_ts accepts now, aware datetimes, or explicit-offset RFC3339 strings.
blocks.title: Store errors and timestamps

blocks.text: db_path resolves state.db without I/O. _secure_database_file opens or creates a regular, user-owned 0600 file, while _secure_sidecars checks SQLite WAL, shared-memory, and journal files.
blocks.title: Database file protection

blocks.text: _configure enables busy timeout, foreign keys, WAL when available, and FULL synchronous mode. connect applies file protection, opens SQLite with explicit transaction control, configures it, and closes on setup failure.
blocks.title: SQLite connection setup

blocks.text: open_db prepares the trusted config directory, connects to state.db, and invokes migrations while ensuring a failed migration closes the connection.
blocks.title: Configured database entry point

blocks.text: transaction takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE outside an existing transaction and commits or rolls back. Inside a transaction it creates a unique savepoint and releases or rolls back that savepoint.
blocks.title: Atomic and nested transaction scopes

gotchas: connect does not migrate; open_db does.
Native Windows is refused by the POSIX permission backstop.
Nested transactions use savepoints and roll back only the inner scope.
how_it_works: Uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE or nested savepoints
purpose: This is the single database-opening module for local sessions, events, approvals, and checkpoints. It secures the database and SQLite sidecars, configures durability and foreign keys, optionally runs migrations, and exposes a composable transaction context manager.
summary: Opens and secures the local SQLite state database and provides atomic transactions.
